readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckActualEvolutionDerivative.hasDerivAt_chartEvolution_of_affine_inner
readback.mathematical_statement: Let E be the fixed ClosedSmoothModel 3 = EuclideanSpace real (Fin 3), with its standard Euclidean norm, Bilin = E ->L[real] (E ->L[real] real), Jet1 = E ->L[real] Bilin, Jet2 = E ->L[real] Jet1, and Variables = (Bilin times Jet1) times Jet2. The displayed letI dictionaries equip every continuous-linear-map carrier, including the background connection and its derivative, with its canonical iterated operator norm and real normed-space structure; the two product layers have their canonical maximum product norm and componentwise addition. They introduce no replacement or rescaled norm. For every universe u and type M : Type u with a topology, T2Space, charts modeled on E, and a smooth IsManifold structure for I = closedSmoothModelWithCorners 3, universally quantify g0,bg : ClosedSmoothRiemannianMetric 3 M, a family gt : real -> ClosedSmoothRiemannianMetric 3 M, and a tangent-bilinear section H assigning each x : M a continuous bilinear real form on TangentSpace I x. These metric objects are genuine smooth Riemannian metrics: their defining carrier includes symmetric positive definite inner forms, von Neumann bounded metric unit balls in the given tangent topology, and smoothness of the metric section. No compactness, connectedness, or completeness of M is assumed by the type or by the word Closed in the abbreviation. Assume H is smooth as a section of the bilinear-form bundle, exactly the displayed ContMDiff I (I.prod the real Bilin model) infinity of x -> TotalSpace.mk' Bilin x (H x). Assume that eventually for s in the real neighborhood filter at zero, for every x : M, inner(gt(s))(x) = inner(g0)(x) + s times H(x). This is one common parameter neighborhood valid simultaneously for all manifold points, rather than separate point-dependent neighborhoods. No derivative of gt is a premise, and no independent parameter or joint regularity of gt is required. For every anchor : M and z : E in the actual target of extChartAt I anchor, also assume the chosen GeodesicTransport.cutoff anchor equals 1 on a neighborhood of z. This cutoff is the fixed smooth blending cutoff; the latter assumption selects its one-region germ, not every point of a chart target. Let C_a(q) be CovariantDerivative.chartMetric q anchor: the unblended coordinate pullback of the tangent-bilinear section q by the inverse extended chart, using its actual manifold differential. Set G0=C_a(inner(g0)), F=C_a(H), DG0=D G0, D2G0=D(D G0), DF=D F, and D2F=D(D F), where D is ordinary real Frechet differentiation in E. Let B be GeodesicTransport.chartChristoffelField bg anchor and DB=D B; this is the Christoffel field of the background metric's blended chart metric, with background bg held fixed. The asserted conclusion is HasDerivAt [s -> deTurckChartMetricEvolutionBilin gt bg anchor s z] [DeTurckJetLinearization.differential (B(z)) (DB(z)) (G0(z)) (DG0(z)) (D2G0(z)) ((F(z),DF(z)),D2F(z))] 0, an ordinary real parameter derivative in the canonical Bilin operator norm. The differentiated function is the actual unblended chart representation of -2 Ricci(gt(s)) + Lie_{W(gt(s),bg)} inner(gt(s)); W is the metric contraction of the difference of the metric and background Levi-Civita connections. To spell out the complete right-hand side, write e_i=basis3(i), A_ij=inverseEntries(G0(z))_ij, J0=DG0(z), K0=D2G0(z), and L_(B,DB)(G,J)=DeTurckPrincipalIdentity.lowerTerm (B(z)) (DB(z)) G J. The derivative is sum over i,j of A_ij times D2F(z)(e_i)(e_j), plus sum over i,j of deltaA_ij times K0(e_i)(e_j), plus D L_(B,DB)(G0(z),J0) applied to (F(z),DF(z)), where deltaA_ij = -sum over k,l of A_ik times F(z)(e_k)(e_l) times A_lj. Thus both inverse factors in the inverse-metric variation and the full lower-term Frechet differential are retained, and neither B nor DB is varied. The family of actual metrics and its affine identity are supplied assumptions; this assertion does not construct such a family, compactly support H, assume a Ricci/DeTurck flow equation, transfer jets under a coordinate change, or prove full covariance. No circular derivative certificate or evolution-derivative hypothesis appears: the conclusion differentiates the defined nonlinear geometric evolution tensor from the stated affine metric variation.
